```js
const a = { d: new Date(), m: new Map([[1, 'x']]), u: undefined };
structuredClone(a);            // Date stays Date, Map stays Map, u kept
JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(a)); // d is a string, m is {}, u dropped
```
structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets and typed arrays and handles circular refs, whereas the JSON round trip only keeps plain JSON values (and throws on cycles). Neither copies functions or class prototypes.

Use `useLayoutEffect` when you must read or change layout before the browser paints, such as measuring an element and setting its position, so the user never sees a flicker. `useEffect` runs after paint and is right for almost everything else (fetching, subscriptions, logging). Note `useLayoutEffect` blocks painting and doesn't run on the server, so it warns during SSR in Next.
